description:
Issue 96 (gh-96) brief: lift the reusable PDF-reader implementation out of src/bin/kpdf.rs into the kopitiam-pdf library, so kovan (and any egui app) can embed the SAME reader kpdf uses, instead of copying from kpdf.rs.

Sizing (kopitiam outline, 2026-08-31 SGT): kpdf.rs is 3899 lines / ~51k tokens, KpdfApp alone has ~60 methods over ~2900 lines. gui_frontend/ already holds 2649 lines of reusable bits (geometry, keys, forms, hit_test, lru, zoom, pixmap, tools, hot_reload).

12 phases in the brief. Maintainer scoped v0.3.2 to the FOUNDATIONS only:
  * Phase 11 - feature split: egui feature separate from kpdf, so an embedder is not forced to pull eframe+rfd. MUST be first, else kovan cannot depend on the reusable half at all.
  * Phase 1  - freeze current behaviour with headless tests before moving anything.
  * Phase 2  - extract RenderWorker/RenderRequest/RenderedPage/RenderKind -> gui_frontend/render.rs
  * Phase 3  - extract SearchWorker + incremental scan state -> gui_frontend/search.rs

Deferred to v0.3.3+: Phase 4 viewport, 5 thumbnails, 6 PdfReader, 7 ReaderAction event boundary, 8 config/capabilities, 10 annotation/form GUI state, 12 kpdf composes the reader.

Maintainer decision recorded up front (shapes phases 5-6): the reader edge is the PAGE PANE ONLY. reader.ui(ui) paints just the document; thumbnails/outline are separate methods the host drops into a Panel it owns. Rationale: egui Panels cannot be created inside a Ui, and kovan needs to own its own layout/splits.

Hard constraints from the brief: no Kovan changes, no Kovan/Markdown/literature/research concepts in the reusable reader, headless build stays headless, no UX rewrite, no big-bang move - every slice compiles and kpdf stays green.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
v0.3.2 landed phases 11, 1-3 of the gh-96 brief.

DONE:
* Phase 11 feature split. New `egui` feature = gui_frontend alone; `kpdf` = egui + eframe + rfd. gui_frontend gated on `egui` not `kpdf`. compile_error! in lib.rs enforces kpdf => egui so they cannot drift. VERIFIED by cargo tree: the egui-only build contains neither eframe nor rfd. All three configs build (--no-default-features, --features egui, default).
* Phase 2 render worker -> gui_frontend/render.rs (430 lines). RenderWorker/RenderRequest/RenderedPage/RenderKind/RenderKey. Was already egui-free (traffics raw RGBA + size), so it moved clean. Field access replaced by methods: generation(), bump_generation(), request(), is_inflight(), busy(), try_recv(). 6 tests incl. equivalence-vs-direct-render and the stale-generation timing guard.
* Phase 3 search worker -> gui_frontend/search.rs (310 lines). SearchWorker + FindScan + scan_page_order(). The backward scan wrap arithmetic is now a pure tested function - it cycles with period n, which my first test expectation got wrong; the test caught me, not the code. 8 tests.
* PageTextureKey in kpdf.rs is now an ALIAS for gui_frontend::RenderKey, so the texture cache and the worker cannot drift on what identifies a page image.
* AID-0057 records the maintainer's reader-boundary call (page pane only; sidebars are host-owned) with alternatives + what would make it wrong.

kpdf.rs: 3899 -> 3481 lines. Gates: 643 lib + 5 bin + 16 integration + 1 doctest green, clippy 0 errors and no NEW warnings (bin now warns 0, was 3), workspace builds.

NEXT (v0.3.3+): Phase 4 viewport, 5 thumbnails, 6 PdfReader, 7 ReaderAction, 8 config, 10 annot/form GUI state, 12 kpdf composes the reader.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
ALL 12 PHASES DONE in v0.3.2.

Phases 11,1,2,3 landed earlier (d7e5a06). This turn added 4,5,6,7,8,9,10,12:

* Phase 4 viewport.rs (Viewport) - slot cache + invalidation, current page recomputed from overlap, scroll intents taken once, 1-based :N conversion in ONE place. egui-free (deltas are (f32,f32)), so 12 headless tests.
* Phase 5 thumbnails.rs (Thumbnails, THUMBNAIL_DPI) - request/get/is_pending engine; the sidebar WIDGET is separate, per AID-0057.
* Phase 6 reader.rs (PdfReader, 2900 lines) - the whole reader. open_bytes/open_bytes_with/load_bytes/document_bytes/document/current_page/page_count/has_unsaved_changes/mark_saved/config/status/set_status/set_label/pump/ui/show.
* Phase 7 action.rs (ReaderAction, PdfReaderOutput) - PageChanged, RegionSelected, AnnotationCreated/Changed, LinkActivated, DocumentModified, SaveRequested, SaveAsRequested, OpenRequested, QuitRequested. Non-exhaustive. NO downstream vocabulary (no DigitiseGraph etc).
* Phase 8 config.rs (PdfReaderConfig + read_only() + can_modify()).
* Phase 9 vim keys stayed in the reader, built on gui_frontend::keys as required.
* Phase 10 annotation/form GUI state moved with the reader.
* Phase 12 kpdf.rs is now a SHELL: 3899 -> 630 lines. Only path, hot_reload, file dialogs, atomic save-via-tmp+rename, eframe lifecycle. Its App::ui is 4 lines: check_hot_reload, reader.show(ui), handle actions.

CORRECTION worth remembering: AID-0057 claimed 'an egui::Panel cannot be created inside a Ui'. FALSE for egui 0.36 - panel.rs:422 is literally 'Show the panel inside a [Ui]', and kpdf had been doing it all along. I asserted an API constraint from memory of an older egui. The DECISION survives on its other leg (host owns layout), and the correction turned an either/or into a layering: ui() is the pane primitive, show() is the chrome convenience on top. AID amended in place with a Correction section (never silently rewritten) + index row updated.

Reader emits QuitRequested instead of send_viewport_cmd(Close) - an embedded reader must not close its host's window. :wq pushes SaveRequested BEFORE QuitRequested; order is contract, pinned by test.

examples/embed_reader.rs is a real third-party host (read-only, own right-hand panel, own event log) compiled by CI - that IS acceptance criterion 1, not a description of it.

Gates: 675 lib (+32) + 9 + 4 + 1 + 2 + 2 doctests green; clippy no new warnings and the pre-existing duplicate-#[test] in geometry.rs fixed; all 3 feature configs build; cargo tree proves 0 eframe/rfd in the egui-only build; workspace clean.

title: kopitiam-pdf: extract kpdf into a reusable embeddable egui reader
